records.description: The twelfth Conference of the Parties to the Nairobi Convention met in Dar es Salaam on 6-9 October 2026 with its ten Contracting Parties. Tanzania set priorities including national law and enforcement, coastal ecosystem restoration and marine pollution. records.description: El Nino, a positive Indian Ocean Dipole and record global ocean temperatures built heat stress across the region from late 2023. CORDIO East Africa reported more than 8 degree heating weeks by February 2024 and over 12 by April, with pockets in Seychelles reaching 16. The 2026 GCRMN regional chapter states that 93% of the region's reefs passed 4 degree heating weeks in 2024-2025 and that values above 20 were documented for the first time.

Before he spoke, Eritrea, Egypt, Somalia and Sudan issued a joint statement saying control of the Red Sea is the exclusive responsibility of the countries that border it. In March 2026 Abiy said Ethiopia would not go to war over sea access.

notes.duration: The Assab question runs from Ethiopia's earlier maritime deal with Somaliland through statements in March and October 2026 (refs 1, 2).

records.description: NOAA's Climate Prediction Center says on 8 October 2026 that El Niño continues to strengthen, with eastern equatorial Pacific sea surface temperatures more than 4.0C above average in places. NOAA's marine heatwave forecast gives eastern tropical Pacific heatwave likelihood above 90% through winter 2026-27, and global coverage is forecast to reach 45%. NOAA Fisheries said on 8 October 2026 that the chance of a very strong El Niño in fall and winter 2026-27 is above 83 percent and that the event is expected to last into early spring 2027, with expected effects on West Coast, Pacific Islands, Alaska and Caribbean fisheries and marine life. Copernicus Climate Change Service reported on 14 October 2026 that September 2026 had the highest September sea surface temperature on record for the extra-polar ocean (60S-60N) at 21.05C, against the previous record of 20.92C in 2023, with record September values along the Atlantic coast and in the western Mediterranean.

records.title: Oil slick and shoreline fuel oil after the 6 October drone attack on the tanker Rio put Krasnodar's Black Sea coast on alert
records.description: After a naval drone attack set the Liberian-flagged Aframax tanker Rio on fire off Sochi on 6 October 2026, satellite monitoring showed a slick spreading along the Krasnodar coast as far as Anapa. Fuel oil was found along about 500 metres of shoreline at Novorossiysk and oiled birds were recovered, and the governor ordered heightened alert for Gelendzhik and Novorossiysk. Regional emergency officials say only small amounts reached the shore and that these did not come from the tanker, while Greenpeace and satellite projects tie the slick to the attack.

notes.significance: Governor Veniamin Kondratyev's order of 13 October raised the alert level for Gelendzhik and Novorossiysk and warned of a potential emergency, a formal notice short of an emergency declaration (refs 1, 2).

records.title: California's Fish and Game Commission approves two new tribally co-led marine protected areas, Mishopshno and Point Sal, after voting on 15 petitions
records.description: California's Fish and Game Commission voted on the remaining 15 marine protected area petitions at its 15 and 16 October 2026 hearings. It approved the Mishopshno State Marine Conservation Area at Carpinteria on a 3-2 vote and a 9.18 square mile Point Sal SMCA, the first new MPA approvals in 12 years, and denied or saw withdrawn proposals for Santa Cruz, the Channel Islands, Cabrillo and Catalina. The Department of Fish and Wildlife had recommended denying all petitions; regulations still have to be written and protections may take a couple of years.

records.title: Revolution Wind: after two stop-work orders and court injunctions, Interior asks a court to remand the project's 2023 construction approval

records.title: International Seabed Authority Council ends July 2026 session in Kingston without adopting the deep-sea mining code
records.description: The ISA Council ended Part II of its 31st session in Kingston, Jamaica, on 24 July 2026 without adopting the exploitation regulations known as the Mining Code. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence reported that environmental safeguards, liability, inspection and benefit-sharing remain unresolved and that experts expect talks to run three to four more years. Over 30 countries have called for a moratorium, and the United States has moved ahead with its own licensing process.

records.title: USGS study finds seafloor sulfide rocks from Escanaba Trough spontaneously combusted during lab processing, raising a mining safety question
records.description: A USGS-led study in Scientific Reports reports that some metal sulfide rocks from Escanaba Trough on the southern Gorda Ridge off the US West Coast spontaneously combusted during laboratory processing. The combusting rocks were mainly nanocrystalline marcasite, and the authors recommend dedicated risk assessments and engineering controls for seafloor massive sulfide mining. The study does not show that all such deposits will combust.
